verdict: American Water's revenue rose 4% to $1.51B on higher regulated rates, and net income rose 2% to $387M — EPS held flat at $1.94 as new shares and higher depreciation absorbed the growth.

kpis.label: Infrastructure invested (9 months)
kpis.note: Pipe replacement and growth, recovered through rates

segments.name: Regulated Businesses
segments.note: Water service ($1,263M: homes $762M, businesses $297M, fire service and others) and wastewater service ($120M) across 14 states, at rates set by regulators.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Water services for military bases and homeowner services such as line protection plans.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of treatment plants and pipes over their lives — it rises with the $2.8B invested so far this year.

opex.name: General taxes
opex.note: Property, payroll and other non-income taxes.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $167M on utility debt, partly offset by interest income, pension credits and $17M of other income.

takeaways.title: Revenue rose to $1.51B
takeaways.text: Higher approved rates and customer growth in the regulated business, which is 93% of revenue.

takeaways.title: EPS flat at $1.94
takeaways.text: Profit grew 2%, but EPS went sideways: more shares outstanding and higher depreciation and interest on new investment ate the increase.

takeaways.title: Investing heavily in pipes
takeaways.text: American Water put $2.8B into infrastructure in nine months — spending that regulators let it earn a return on through future rates.

footerNote: Operation and maintenance ($531M as reported) is treated as the direct cost of producing and delivering water, shown net of a $1M other operating credit. AWK reports no separate cost-of-revenue line.
